subject: Problems with predicted abundance values in DSM

messages.author: 3cc57783657c133b
messages.subject: Problems with predicted abundance values in DSM
parts:
Dear colleagues,

I need your help again.
I have fitted several GAM models (unit to model: subsample; object to model:
clusters; response variable: abundance; error distribution: quasipuason;
observation weights: none) using DSM analysis engine. They differ with data
filters and formulas used. The models explain from 29 to 64% (For example,
one of them: R-sq.(adj) = 0.276; Deviance explained = 46.3%; GCV score =
2.4883; Scale est. = 2.4274; n = 4076).
However, when I use these models for predictions, I get unrealistically low
predicted values (for example, all predicted values for the model above are
between 1.78682671764E-10 and 1.05191835321E-05 while I expected them to be
somewhere between 0 and few thousands as the count data are). Initially I
thought that the problem is in measurement units, so I checked that area for
the study area and strata are in square meters and length of transects and
sections is in meters. Also in Data filter properties window the units are
meters and square meters. I tried also changing the "Grid cell area" field
in the Prediction tab of the Model definition properties window, however,
this did not affect the predicted values and only total abundance in study
area values changed.
When I visualise the result in GIS, I can see that preditions reflect
relative abundance quite well (i.e. values are indeed higher where I
expected them to be) so visually the maps look nice (if used without
legend:).
Any ideas what might be wrong? Have I forgotten to set meters/square meters
somewhere? Or does the problem lay in the fitted models (the distribution of
residuals is not symmetrical around zero, more residuals are below 0)? Or it
is rather the prediction grid that cause the problem? Or smth else?
